title: Your team needs an andon cord
summary: Our startup's (selective) embrace of some hardcore DevOps principles.
body_text: Alexander Belanger Co-Founder Hatchet One of the most important engineering decisions we made this year was sending the following emoji in our company Slack channel. If you’d told me that 2 years ago, I probably would’ve quit on the spot; assuming, naturally, that the shitcoiners trying to infiltrate our Discord had done so successfully and I was an NFT shill. But this is not that. The green toad is called Bufo, and the yellow rope-looking thing is an andon cord. Stay with me. What’s an andon cord? It’s an actual, physical rope, originally used in Japan’s manufacturing industry, most notably Toyota factories, and popularized in Western culture through Mike Rother’s Toyota Kata . In the event of a defect, bottleneck, or other known issue in a factory, an employee would pull the andon cord and all factory production would stop. Please excuse the AI-generated image; I couldn’t find a fair-use picture of an andon cord on the internet. There’s no point in continuing production if a bottleneck exists in the assembly line, because the productivity losses caused by the bottleneck (backpressure on upstream components, underutilization of downstream components) would exceed those caused by fully stopping production to fix the issue. Productivity gains aside, the andon cord has a significant cultural utility: it reinforces continuous improvement and discourages the normalization of production issues. What does this have to do with software? In Hatchet’s early days, we spoke often of the kind of culture we’d like to build. One of our founding team members mentioned the andon cord as a cultural norm they’d appreciated in a previous job. It immediately resonated with us. Every software startup is a factory. The raw materials are computers, human brains, and your other tooling. The output is software delivered to end users. Our assembly line involves a lot of steps. Writing code is a small part of the process: gathering user feedback, getting feedback internally, reviewing PRs, staging deployments, load tests, and production rollouts comprise the bulk of the work. Anything that impacts our ability to ship and deploy a stable, reliable platform impacts the performance of our factory, and therefore, our bottom line. We decided that slowdowns or bottlenecks in our factory would be the overriding priority. And thus, :bufo-pulls-the-andon-cord: was born. When everything’s highest priority, nothing is Note the emphasis on overriding priority. We’re an ambitious team, so we tend to bite off a lot of work at once. When a customer asks for something, and we think it’s a great feature request, we usually make it a priority. When we notice a small spike in latency on some critical-path service, we also make it a priority. When we postmortem an outage, it’s the priority. And so on, until the priority tickets pile up. In a world of hundreds of high-priority tickets, it becomes impossible to see through the noise. You’re constantly shipping, fighting fires, and feeling like you’re falling behind. The andon cord makes the ultimate priority very clear: there is nothing more important than our ability to ship reliable software. A clear and resolvable problem in our software factory is more important than anything else (yes, even new features and launches). It’s worth stopping all work to resolve it. It’s slightly counterintuitive: you would think that throwing a signal interrupt every few weeks would lead to more noise and overhead. And in the short term, this is true. But after a few months of resolving the most critical bottlenecks, you suddenly start to be able to ship with fewer fires and less unplanned work. Our andon cord-worthy problems I won’t bore you with the deep internals of Hatchet’s factory, but it’s worth listing the cases where we’ve pulled the andon cord in the past 6 months. For some background on our infrastructure setup, Hatchet runs on over 25 shards in 3 regions. Our busiest shards are running tens of thousands of transactions per second. This volume naturally makes certain things difficult. We didn’t have a sensible rollout strategy, leading to releases piling up in our backlog, and multiple big risky changes being shipped simultaneously. Before continuing deployments, we rewrote our entire deployment process. We didn’t have good enough observability, so customers alerted us about unexpected latency before we were aware of it. We started very closely tracking latency metrics and instrumented all critical-path endpoints. We had a ton of observability data, but we were over-alerting and over-paging. We stopped all work to move towards zero error logs in production. Our staging environment wasn’t catching enough issues during the load testing process. We rolled out a new environment called staging-chonky and rewrote our load testing harness. These days, we still have andon cord moments, but they’re resolved very quickly, and usually by one or two team members, instead of the entire team. We’ve ramped up our shipping velocity significantly in the past few months; this past week, we shipped 3 new core engine features, and a ton of smaller improvements and fixes. The burden of unplanned work Can you tell we’ve been reading The Phoenix Project? At startups, there’s a continuous pressure to ship all of the time. Dropping everything to invest in our tooling and process is rare among startups that I talk to; most teams tend to normalize and adopt the mentality that “things are on fire because we’re a startup.” The issue is that there is nothing more burdensome than unplanned work, and it’s usually invisible to teams when it becomes normalized. This unplanned work regularly produces heroic, monumental efforts—like pulling an all-nighter to resolve some critical incident—which just leads to more pressure to meet tight deadlines, which leads to more unplanned work, and so on. I used to think this was just part of startup culture. But adopting and implementing the andon cord principle has changed my view significantly. There’s short-term pain, yes; but by honoring the andon cord, we’re shipping rapidly and more effectively now. PostScript: Bufo has PMF An aside to the aside: Bufo is a genus of true toads in the amphibian family Bufonidae. This post is not about Bufo, but at this point you might be wondering who he is. We provide a lot of customer support through shared Slack channels. These are Slack channels which are connected from one workspace to another. This also means that we get to see which emojis other companies are using. Earlier this year, we started seeing this little toad emoji reacting to various messages in our Slack channel. I only know of 2 named toads: Toad from Frog & Toad , and Pepe. Pepe was born out of 4chan, the birthplace of incel culture, and in my mind has a fairly negative connotation. Thankfully, a quick google search revealed that this is a different green toad called Bufo. Within a week of seeing Bufo, he appeared in our internal emoji set, much to the chagrin of our overly curmudgeonly head of growth, who attempted her own andon cord moment of sorts: It didn’t work. And within a few months, Bufo had successfully infiltrated at least five other shared Slack channels. I’ve never seen clearer signs of product-market fit.

title: Translating Clinical Guidance Into Coverage Policy
summary: Learn how the PLUGS Prenatal Exome and Genome Sequencing Policy helps health plans translate evolving clinical evidence into clear coverage criteria.
body_text: PLUGS POLICY ‍ Patient-centered Laboratory Utilization Guidance Services (PLUGS) ‍ ‍ Prenatal Exome and Genome Sequencing Policy ‍ Read the full PLUGS policy Key Takeaways The PLUGS Prenatal Exome and Genome Sequencing Policy provides health plans with an evidence-based foundation for medical policy development. The policy translates professional society guidance and published evidence into clearly defined coverage criteria. Earlier access to prenatal ES/GS may support diagnosis before birth and inform pregnancy management, delivery planning, neonatal preparedness, and coordinated care. Clear criteria can support more consistent coverage decisions, appropriate utilization, and reduced administrative burden. Translating Prenatal Genomic Sequencing Guidance Into Coverage Policy Recent guidance from the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM) reinforces the expanding clinical role of prenatal exome and genome sequencing in selected high-risk pregnancies. While professional society guidance informs clinical practice, health plans must determine how those recommendations should be translated into clear, evidence-based medical policy. The PLUGS Prenatal Exome and Genome Sequencing Policy bridges that gap by translating current clinical guidance and published evidence into clearly defined medical policy criteria. Developed through a rigorous review of the medical literature and discussion with subject matter experts, the policy provides health plans with an expert-developed, evidence-based foundation they can adopt to streamline medical policy development and support consistent coverage decisions. Why the PLUGS Prenatal Exome and Genome Sequencing Policy Matters Patient-centered Laboratory Utilization Guidance Services (PLUGS) is a national laboratory stewardship collaborative that brings together health systems, laboratories, clinicians, payors, industry, and patient advocacy organizations to improve access to medically appropriate laboratory testing. One of PLUGS' core priorities is Insurance Alignment, developing evidence-based medical policies and best-practice recommendations that help standardize coverage criteria, reduce administrative burden, and improve access to medically necessary testing. This collaborative approach ensures policies are grounded in current evidence while reflecting the practical considerations of real-world coverage policy development. Key Elements of the Prenatal Exome and Genome Sequencing Policy The PLUGS Prenatal Exome and Genome Sequencing Policy provides health plans with clearly defined medical policy criteria informed by current clinical guidance. Key elements include: Defining Appropriate Use The policy identifies the clinical scenarios where prenatal exome and genome sequencing may be appropriate, helping health plans establish consistent medical necessity criteria for patients most likely to benefit. Establishing Clear Coverage Criteria The policy outlines when prenatal exome and genome sequencing should be considered, providing health plans with clear, evidence-based criteria that support consistent coverage decisions. Supporting Clinically Meaningful Outcomes The policy focuses on situations where a prenatal genetic diagnosis has the potential to influence clinical decision-making, including pregnancy management, delivery planning, neonatal care, and family counseling. Promoting Consistent Policy Application By translating published evidence and professional society recommendations into defined medical policy criteria, the policy helps health plans promote appropriate utilization while reducing unnecessary variation in coverage decisions. Why Earlier Access to Prenatal Genomic Sequencing Matters for Health Plans The timing of a diagnosis is often influenced by the timing of access to testing. Medical policies do more than define coverage; rather, they help determine when patients receive answers that can inform clinical care. For pregnancies with suspected genetic conditions, access to prenatal exome and genome sequencing may provide opportunities to establish a diagnosis before birth rather than once a critically ill newborn requires evaluation. Earlier diagnosis can support informed pregnancy management, delivery planning at an appropriate facility, neonatal preparedness, and coordinated care from the moment a child is born. For health plans, these decisions have implications beyond medical policy. Earlier diagnostic clarity may reduce diagnostic uncertainty after birth, minimize sequential genetic testing, support more coordinated specialty care, and help clinicians prepare for an infant's medical needs before delivery. While every case is unique, policies that support appropriate use of prenatal genomic sequencing have the potential to shift care from reactive evaluation after birth to proactive planning before delivery. Continue the Conversation As prenatal genomic sequencing continues to evolve, GeneDx is committed to helping health plans evaluate emerging clinical evidence and its implications for medical policy. Whether your organization is developing a new prenatal genomic sequencing policy or reassessing existing coverage criteria, the GeneDx Market Access team can help. title: HPE: Accelerating High-Performance Computing Through Smarter Tools and Collaboration
summary: Learn how HPE boosts HPC chip development with Synopsys tools, elastic compute resources, streamlined verification, and AI-driven workflows.
body_text: Behind the world’s fastest supercomputers is an enormous amount of unseen engineering mastery. Chips must be designed, verified, and delivered on tight schedules. Expertise and resources are often limited. And complexity continues to rise. For Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), that challenge is especially acute within the Slingshot organization, which develops the high‑speed interconnect fabric that powers leading high‑performance computing (HPC) systems. David Lacey, a distinguished technologist at HPE, sits at the intersection of engineering, methodology, and technology strategy. Trained as a verification engineer, he now works across teams to improve productivity, evaluate new technologies, and ensure that Slingshot silicon meets both quality and schedule goals. “My role gives me the opportunity to work across pretty much all of our teams,” Lacey says. “That includes guiding how we improve our methodologies, integrate new technologies, and ultimately deliver new generations of Slingshot chips.” Evaluating technology through a productivity lens New tools and techniques arrive constantly in semiconductor design, but Lacey’s team takes a disciplined approach when deciding what to adopt. “We look at what the technology is going to do for us,” he explains. “But we also look at what it’s going to take to integrate it into our workflows.” That integration effort can be significant. Tools often need to be automated, connected to existing systems, and made usable across large engineering teams. Cost, effort, and expected return all factor into the final decision. “If it’s a good return on investment and it helps us drive quality into our chips or pull in our schedules, then it’s something we look at very seriously,” Lacey says. A longstanding collaboration with Synopsys Many of these decisions are made in collaboration with Synopsys, which has been part of HPE’s design environment since the days of Cray supercomputers. That history spans multiple generations of Slingshot development. “We’ve used Synopsys tools for many years,” Lacey says. “That continuity creates a very strong working relationship.” Today, the Slingshot team uses Synopsys tools across the entire design flow, from front‑end development through back‑end implementation. For verification, simulation remains the workhorse, complemented by formal verification and emulation to form a comprehensive methodology focused on first‑pass silicon success. “All of those pieces together are essential to getting high‑quality chips out the door,” Lacey notes. Image courtesy HPE Bringing cloud-like flexibility on-premises One recent outcome of HPE’s collaboration with Synopsys is the certification of HPE GreenLake Flex for use with Synopsys FlexEDA Pay‑Per‑Use (PPU) licensing . Previously, that specific deployment option was limited to public cloud environments, which can pose challenges for teams with strict security and intellectual property requirements. The newly certified solution gives engineering teams elastic, cloud‑like compute capacity while allowing them to keep workloads on-premises. “Many teams can’t use the public cloud,” Lacey says. “This approach lets them take advantage of pay‑per‑use licensing and elastic compute, while still controlling all the security around their IP.” The most immediate benefit shows up in turnaround time. Faster access to compute means results come back sooner, enabling engineers to respond more quickly. “We might get regression results overnight instead of waiting 24 hours,” he explains. “That allows engineers to act right away instead of switching to something else.” Turning faster feedback into schedule gains Shorter turnaround times do more than save hours, Lacey says. “When results take a full day, people naturally move on to other tasks,” he explains. “When the results finally arrive, you have to mentally switch back.” Reducing that friction keeps engineers focused and helps quality improvements happen earlier in the design cycle. Over time, those gains can add up to meaningful schedule acceleration, especially in environments where staffing is tight and timelines are aggressive. “Our challenges aren’t unique,” Lacey says. “Time to market and limited resources are things a lot of teams face. The question is how tools help engineers get more done in the time they have.” Image courtesy HPE Leaning into AI-driven engineering As EDA tools continue to evolve, Lacey sees artificial intelligence playing an increasingly important role. He describes the industry as being at an early stage, with much more potential ahead. “We’re just scratching the surface of what AI technologies can do,” he says, pointing to advances in generative and agent‑based systems that can reason through complex workflows. The goal is not to replace engineers, Lacey emphasizes, but to change how they spend their time. “We want computers handling the more mundane tasks,” he says. “That frees engineers to focus on the things only humans can do.” Powering systems with real-world impact The stakes are high. Slingshot fabrics power some of the fastest computers in the world — systems used for weather forecasting, healthcare research, automotive safety analysis, and other applications that directly affect daily life. “That’s what makes this work meaningful,” Lacey says. “These systems enable research that helps humanity.” Faster design cycles and higher-quality silicon are means to an end. For the HPE Slingshot team, that work ultimately supports the researchers, scientists, and engineers using some of the world's most powerful computing systems. Asset Management FRE1 decreased to $1.4 million from $2.2 million in the prior year quarter, but increased $0.2 million from first quarter 2026 FRE of $2.6 million and SRE of $4.9 million for the first half of 2026, resulting in Segment Income of $7.5 million1 representing a 69% increase, or $3.1 million, as compared to the prior year period Mount Logan continues to make progress on key strategic and operational initiatives including its insurance growth strategy, whereby Ability received its B+ AM Best Rating after quarter-end After quarter-end, the pending Yieldstreet Alternative Income Fund transaction received the requisite approvals and is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026 NEW YORK, Aug. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mount Logan Capital Inc. (Nasdaq: MLCI) (“Mount Logan” or the “Company”) announced today its financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Management Commentary Ted Goldthorpe, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Mount Logan stated, “Sequential improvement in Segment Income reflects the progress we are making as we increase scale, control costs, and execute against our growth initiatives. Ability's investment-grade rating from AM Best, together with the pending Yieldstreet transaction, marks meaningful progress in unlocking the earnings potential of our integrated asset management and insurance platform. We believe Mount Logan is well positioned to generate durable earnings growth and long-term shareholder value in the quarters ahead.” Second Quarter Financial and Business Highlights 2 Total revenue for the Asset Management segment was $2.3 million for the quarter, a decrease of $1.1 million, or 32% compared to the second quarter of 2025. Asset Management revenues exclude $1.6 million of intercompany management fees earned from managing the assets of Ability Insurance Company ("Ability"), which remained flat from the same 2025 period. Fee-Related Earnings (“FRE”) for the Asset Management segment were $1.4 million for the second quarter of 2026, down $0.9 million compared to $2.2 million for the second quarter of 2025. Total net investment income for the Insurance Solutions segment including net investment income of consolidated variable interest entities ("VIEs") was $18.5 million for the second quarter of 2026, a decrease of $2.0 million, or 10%, compared to second quarter of 2025. Excluding the funds withheld assets under reinsurance contracts and modified coinsurance ("Modco") arrangements, the Insurance Solutions segment’s net investment income was $13.0 million, a decrease of $0.1 million, or 1%, compared to the second quarter of 2025. Achieved a 6.2% 3 yield on the insurance investment portfolio for the second quarter of 2026. Excluding the funds withheld under reinsurance contracts and modified coinsurance, the yield was 6.6%. Spread-Related Earnings (“SRE”) for the Insurance Solutions segment was $2.9 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to ($0.1) million for the second quarter of 2025. Mount Logan's total assets under management ("AUM") was $2.0 billion as of June 30, 2026 and is inclusive of Ability’s assets managed by Mount Logan. Ability's assets excluding intangible assets and the funds withheld assets under reinsurance contracts and Modco, were $784.5 million as of June 30, 2026, a decrease of $6.7 million from the second quarter of 2025. As of June 30, 2026, the Insurance Solutions segment held approximately $1.0 billion of total investment assets, an increase of $28.5 million from the second quarter of 2025. Including Modco assets, Ability's total assets managed by Mount Logan is $953.0 million, an increase of $126.0 million compared to second quarter of 2025. Subsequent Events and Strategic Updates AM Best, a leading, global credit rating agency specializing in the insurance industry, assigned a Financial Strength Rating of B+ “(Good)” and a Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of bbb- “(Good)” to the Company's wholly-owned life and annuity insurance subsidiary, Ability. As previously announced, Mount Logan–managed Opportunistic Credit Interval Fund (“SOFIX”) signed a definitive agreement to acquire $100+ million of assets from Yieldstreet Alternative Income Fund Inc. (“YS AIF”), which is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals, and is estimated to increase FRE by $2.8 million4 or more on a full year basis. On July 31, 2026, Yieldstreet's shareholders voted in favor of the transaction. Declared a stockholder quarterly distribution in the amount of $0.03 per share of common stock for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, payable on August 31, 2026 to stockholders of record at the close of business on August 21, 2026. This cash dividend marks the fourth consecutive quarter of the Company issuing a $0.03 distribution to its stockholders following the closing of the Business Combination. Selected Financial Highlights Total capital of the Company was $171.1 million at June 30, 2026, a decrease of $14.2 million as compared to December 31, 2025. Total capital consists of debt obligations and total shareholders’ equity. Consolidated net loss before taxes was $4.2 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared with a loss of $0.9 million for the second quarter of 2025. Net loss position widened primarily due to net realized and change in unrealized losses from investments in Insurance Solutions. Consolidated basic loss per share (“EPS”) was $0.37 for the second quarter of 2026, compared to $0.14 for the second quarter of 2025. All participants are encouraged to dial in 10 minutes prior to the start time. A replay of the conference call and webcast will be available on-demand via the Company’s investor relations webpage at https://ir.mountlogan.com/ for 12 months. title: EMPLOYERS Appoints Kirt Dooley as Senior Vice President, Chief Actuary
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Employers Holdings, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Actuarial executive brings deep reserving, pricing, and data science expertise to EMPLOYERS leadership team RENO, Nev., Aug. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- EMPLOYERS (NYSE: EIG), a leading provider of workers' compensation insurance solutions for America's small and mid-sized businesses, today announced the appointment of Kirt Dooley as Senior Vice President, Chief Actuary. Dooley joins EMPLOYERS from Clear Spring Property & Casualty Company, where he has served since 2020 as Chief Actuary and Chief Risk Officer, leading the company's actuarial, analytics, and enterprise risk management functions. During his tenure, he built the company's actuarial and data analytics department from the ground up and led a reinsurance business development strategy that grew assumed reinsurance premiums by more than 200 percent over a two-year period. Earlier in his career, Dooley spent 16 years at the National Council on Compensation Insurance (NCCI), most recently as Practice Leader and Senior Actuary, where he led analytical initiatives for regulators and industry stakeholders and represented the organization in regulatory hearings through expert testimony. "Kirt is an accomplished actuary and proven leader whose experience building analytics capabilities will help us continue to manage risk with the consistency and precision that define our company,” said Katherine Antonello, president and chief executive officer of EMPLOYERS. “His background across reserving, pricing, and data science makes him well positioned to lead the next stage of that work." Dooley is a Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society (FCAS) and a member of the American Academy of Actuaries (MAAA). He holds a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics and a Bachelor of Arts in Economics, both from the University of Florida. "EMPLOYERS has built a reputation for financial strength and disciplined underwriting in workers' compensation," said Dooley. "That combination of specialty focus and stability gives the actuarial function meaningful influence over how the business performs. That is the foundation I plan to build on, and I am looking forward to the opportunity to help shape what comes next." About EMPLOYERS Employers Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: EIG), is a holding company with subsidiaries that are specialty providers of workers’ compensation insurance, excess workers’ compensation, and related services (collectively “EMPLOYERS®”) focused on small and mid-sized businesses engaged in lower hazard industries with its guaranteed cost product and self-insured enterprises with its excess workers’ compensation product. EMPLOYERS leverages over a century of experience to deliver comprehensive coverage solutions that meet the unique needs of its customers. Drawing from its long history and extensive knowledge, EMPLOYERS empowers businesses by protecting their most valuable asset , their employees , through exceptional claims management, loss control, and risk management services, to help businesses create safer work environments. EMPLOYERS is also proud to offer Cerity®, which is focused on providing digital-first, direct-to-consumer workers’ compensation insurance solutions with fast and affordable coverage options through a user-friendly online platform. EMPLOYERS operates throughout the United States, apart from four states that are served exclusively by their state funds. Workers’ Compensation insurance is offered through Employers Insurance Company of Nevada, Employers Compensation Insurance Company, Employers Preferred Insurance Company, Employers Assurance Company, and Cerity Insurance Company, and Excess Workers’ Compensation is offered through Employers Assurance Company. Each of EMPLOYERS insurance subsidiaries is rated A (Excellent) by AM Best. Not all companies do business in all jurisdictions. EIG Services, Inc., and Cerity Services, Inc., are subsidiaries of Employers Holdings, Inc. EMPLOYERS® is a registered trademark of EIG Services, Inc., and Cerity® is a registered trademark of Cerity Services, Inc. For more information, please visit www.employers.com , www.employers.com/excess-workers-compensation/ , and www.cerity.com . title: Entergy Louisiana recognized as finalists across multiple 2026 Louisiana Energy Awards categories
summary: Entergy Louisiana has been recognized in three categories as Business Report’s 10/12 Industry Report announced its 2026 Louisiana Energy Awards finalists, reflecting the company’s leadership in…
body_text: Entergy Louisiana has been recognized in three categories as Business Report’s 10/12 Industry Report announced its 2026 Louisiana Energy Awards finalists , reflecting the company’s leadership in resiliency, economic development and strategic planning. Entergy Louisiana is a finalist for Large Energy Company of the Year, honoring its more than 100 years of service, a workforce of approximately 4,500 employees statewide, and major investments including a nearly $2 billion resiliency plan and support for groundbreaking projects with partners such as Meta, Hut8 and Hyundai Steel. The company is also a finalist for Energy Deal of the Year for its role in enabling Hyundai Motor Group’s $5.8 billion decision to build its first North American steel facility in Donaldsonville – made possible through significant generation and transmission upgrades supporting an electric arc furnace mill designed to produce lower‑emission, high‑volume steel. Additionally, Laura Beauchamp, Entergy Louisiana’s vice president of business operations and strategy, has been named a finalist for Emerging Energy Leader of the Year. Her 24‑year career with the company includes leading major strategic initiatives that balance reliability, affordability and environmental stewardship, as well as infrastructure planning to power projects such as Meta’s AI data center, Hyundai Steel, and the First Solar facility in New Iberia. Winners will be announced at the Louisiana Energy Awards celebration on Nov. 18 in Baton Rouge. A full list of this year’s finalists can be found here . About Entergy Louisiana Entergy Louisiana provides electricity to more than 1.1 million customers in 58 parishes. Entergy Louisiana is a subsidiary of Entergy Corporation (NYSE: ETR). Entergy generates, transmits and distributes electricity to power life for 3 million customers through our operating companies in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas. We’re focused on keeping costs for our customers as low as possible while providing reliable energy that our communities count on. We’re also investing in growth for the future with a more resilient, cleaner energy system that includes modern natural gas, nuclear and renewable energy generation. As a nationally recognized leader in sustainability and corporate citizenship, Entergy delivers more than $100 million in economic benefits each year to the communities we serve through philanthropy, volunteerism and advocacy. Entergy is a Fortune 500 company headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, and has approximately 12,000 employees. Learn more at EntergyLouisiana.com and connect with @EntergyLA on social media.

title: CRM Project Management: 13 Best Platforms (Features, Pricing & Focus for 2026)
summary: CRM project management tools compared: features, pricing, and which fits complex workflows. See hidden costs. And when a custom CRM solution is smarter.
body_text: TL;DR: The best CRM project management tools in 2026, Productive, Hubspot, Insightly, Flowlu, Monday, Zoho, and Miniloop, differ in features, pricing, and implementation flexibility; teams with complex workflows or high user counts often save more long-term with a custom CRM like Miniloop. CRM Project Management: 13 Best Platforms (Features, Pricing & Focus for 2026) Last updated: August 2026 The top crm project management are Productive (Best for unified CRM project management), HubSpot (Best for complex needs), Monday.com (Best for work organization), Insightly (Best for managing the full customer journey), Miniloop (Best for custom workflows & cost savings). Project management CRM platforms now span far beyond basic task tracking: as of 2026, even mid-sized organizations are struggling with tool sprawl, rising per-user fees, and rigid features that don’t map to real business workflows. With the latest launches, several tools have doubled down on visual pipeline features and deeper project-sales integration, but pricing complexity and true workflow customization remain pain points for buyers. Leaders evaluating options see frequent trade-offs between usability, cost, and flexibility. Making transparency and fit for unique operations more urgent than ever. What defines a strong CRM project management solution in 2026? A strong CRM project management tool enables businesses to unify deal tracking, task management, client communication, and execution workflows under one roof. But in 2026, picking the right platform is less about slick visuals or popular integrations; it’s about aligning the software to real business processes. And controlling costs as team and project complexity grows. Platforms like Productive and HubSpot lead with broad feature sets and integrations but, for teams with high CRM spend or custom workflows, generic solutions often require expensive workarounds. That’s why buyers should now weigh flexibility, true cost structure, and data ownership as heavily as advertised features. How CRM and project management platforms are converging Modern CRMs and project management platforms are merging into unified systems, increasingly expected by businesses to connect every stage of the customer lifecycle with internal delivery work. This convergence has reshaped software buying criteria in 2026: teams now look for platforms where sales pipelines, project tasks, files, real-time communication, and client-facing activities live in a single environment. The line that once separated customer data management from project execution is fading, with buyers viewing integration as a baseline feature, not an upgrade. Traditionally, CRMs and project management tools operated in distinct silos. CRMs focused on managing leads, contact histories, sales pipelines, and customer records, while project management tools organized internal tasks, deadlines, files, and team collaboration. A sales rep would log opportunity updates in a CRM and hand off closed deals to a project manager, who coordinated execution using an entirely separate system. This disconnect often created friction: information was double-entered or lost, handoffs became bottlenecks, and customers noticed the gap when their onboarding, service, or delivery experiences felt fragmented. Several forces are driving the fusion of these platforms. Businesses increasingly recognize that the customer journey doesn’t end at the sale. It continues through onboarding, delivery, ongoing support, and renewal. Client expectations for responsiveness and transparency mean that any missed detail in a handoff threatens satisfaction. As projects grow complex and teams span multiple functions, organizations require tighter alignment between customer-facing processes and internal workstreams. To meet these demands, leading tools now link pipeline management, project tasks, document storage, and team communication within a single platform. For example, many platforms let users convert won deals directly into projects without rekeying information, ensuring context and files carry over. Comment threads, shared notes, and real-time status updates travel with a customer whether they’re being prospected, onboarded, or supported post-sale. Solutions such as Productive and Monday.com offer visual dashboards that blend client pipeline analytics with project health metrics, enabling leadership to watch both revenue forecasts and delivery schedules side by side. Buyers’ expectations have shifted accordingly. In 2026, teams expect customizable dashboards that span the sales funnel through to project completion. Built-in task automation has become table stakes, automating repetitive actions like follow-up reminders, task assignment after deal closures, and syncing client communication logs between modules. Deep collaboration is also essential: platforms increasingly allow internal users and even clients to discuss files, approve milestones, and track issues within the same workspace, reducing context switching and email chains. title: DARPA, Array Labs Extends Contract for Distributed Radar Architecture
summary: Array Labs is working to provide high-quality 3D imagery on a global scale.
body_text: APRIL 16, 2026, Redwood City, CA & Arlington, VA – The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has extended its contract with Array Labs, adding scope to an existing contract focused on the company’s distributed radar architecture. Building on the original contract, the extension covers modeling and simulation of Array's multistatic radar system, advancing additional analysis on how formation-flying radar satellites perform when operating as a coordinated cluster across a wider range of scenarios. Array’s constellation is designed around a distributed architecture of multiple satellites cooperatively functioning from different orbital positions. "This lets us push deeper into operating modes that only exist when you have multiple radar satellites working as one system,” said Array Labs CEO and Cofounder Andrew Peterson. “We're grateful to be able explore this approach further under this extended contract with DARPA." Array Labs has secured multiple government contracts over the past two years, including awards from the Department of the Air Force (DAF), Office of Naval Research (ONR) the United States Special Operations Command (SOCOM), Office of Department of War, Research and Engineering (OUSW R&E), in addition to DARPA. The company announced a $20M Series A in January 2026.

The platform converts Slack threads and DMs into trackable tickets without disrupting natural conversation flow, allowing employees to request help exactly where they already communicate. Price: Basic: $50/agent/month, Pro: $75/agent/month, Enterprise: Custom G2 Rating: 4.9/5 What Sets Unthread Apart Unthread operates entirely within Slack, eliminating the need for employees to switch between communication and ticketing platforms. The AI automation capabilities handle routing, resolution, and workflow orchestration automatically. Lemonade's Head of IT Danny Fang reports: "Unthread automatically resolves about 40% of all tickets that come in across different teams. This means countless hours saved for employees across the organization." Key Features Purpose-built AI agents for automatic resolution, with Lemonade reporting that Unthread resolves about 40% of tickets across its IT, HR, legal, procurement, and finance teams Self-learning knowledge base that detects repeat questions and drafts help articles from resolved tickets Private ticketing for sensitive HR requests including payroll, parental leave, and employee documents Automation builder supporting natural language, visual workflows, and custom code integrations MCP integrations that allow compatible AI assistants to securely access supported Unthread workspace data and actions Who Should Consider Unthread Remote-first organizations running internal support for IT, HR, finance, legal, and procurement teams within Slack benefit from Unthread's conversational ticketing approach. The ability to turn any Slack channel like #it-help into a full internal help desk with structured ticketing, routing, and SLA tracking resonates with teams seeking to eliminate tool-switching friction. 2) ServiceNow ServiceNow provides cross-departmental service management capabilities with Now Assist generative AI for case summarization, knowledge generation, and workflow automation. ServiceNow's announced acquisition of Moveworks reflects its continued investment in conversational AI and employee service automation. G2 Rating: 4.4/5 ServiceNow's Primary Focus Large organizations with thousands of employees requiring service management across IT, HR, facilities, and finance departments often evaluate ServiceNow for its breadth of ITIL-aligned workflows and deep customization options. Key Capabilities Now Assist generative AI for case summarization and knowledge generation Cross-departmental ITSM workflows covering IT, HR, facilities, and finance Extensive ITIL capabilities and customization options Moveworks integration bringing conversational AI capabilities ServiceNow Implementation Considerations Large, multi-module ServiceNow deployments can take several months and may require implementation partners, although timelines vary substantially by scope and organizational complexity. Custom quote pricing depends on edition, modules, user types, implementation scope, and contract terms. 3) Freshservice Freshservice delivers ITIL-aligned workflows with Freddy AI handling automated responses, self-service, and intelligent routing. The platform is widely used by IT teams and is positioned as a more accessible deployment option than many large enterprise ITSM platforms. G2 Rating: 4.6/5 Freshservice's Core Positioning Mid-sized IT teams needing structured ITSM processes evaluate Freshservice for its balance of feature depth and deployment speed measured in weeks rather than months. Key Capabilities Freddy AI assistant for automated responses, ticket classification, and routing ITIL-aligned workflows covering incident, problem, change, and request management Asset management and configuration database 14-day free trial Consideration: IT-focused rather than multi-department; HR and finance teams may need separate solutions or workarounds. 4) Jira Service Management Jira Service Management offers ITIL-aligned workflows with a free tier supporting up to 3 agents. The platform integrates with Jira Software and Confluence for organizations already using Atlassian products. G2 Rating: 4.2/5 Jira Service Management's Integration Approach Engineering-led IT departments using Atlassian tools evaluate Jira Service Management for service desk capabilities linked to development workflows. Free tier access for up to 3 agents; Standard starts around $20/agent/month and Premium around $51/agent/month, depending on billing terms and team size. Key Capabilities ITIL-aligned workflows for incident, problem, change, and request management Atlassian Assist virtual service agent for Slack and Teams Integration with Jira Software for linking support tickets to development issues Confluence integration for knowledge base management Consideration: Advanced searches and highly customized reporting may require familiarity with JQL or additional configuration. 5) Zendesk Zendesk provides pre-trained AI models built on extensive real-world ticket data for organizations needing cross-departmental service desk capabilities. The platform promotes AI agents for automating eligible support interactions and offers omnichannel coverage, although actual automation rates vary by workflow, knowledge quality, and implementation. G2 Rating: 4.3/5 Zendesk's Market Position Large organizations requiring cross-departmental ITSM with potential integration to external customer support channels evaluate Zendesk for its breadth of automation capabilities and extensive integration ecosystem with over 1,000 available integrations. Key Capabilities AI agents pre-trained on extensive real-world ticket data Omnichannel support across email, chat, voice, and social platforms Extensive app marketplace Workforce management and quality assurance tools Consideration: Requires employees to access a separate portal rather than working within Slack natively, which creates context-switching overhead for remote teams. 6) NinjaOne NinjaOne combines ticketing with RMM (Remote Monitoring and Management), patching, scripting, and remote access capabilities. The platform has received strong user ratings and is commonly evaluated for endpoint management, remote monitoring, and IT operations. NinjaOne's Unified Approach IT teams managing distributed device fleets evaluate NinjaOne for ticketing integrated with endpoint management, device health monitoring, and remote access from a unified console. Key Capabilities Ticketing integrated with device health, scripting, and remote access Automated ticket creation from monitoring alerts Client portal for end-user visibility into ticket status Scripting library for automation Consideration: Per-endpoint pricing works well for device-heavy environments but may not suit organizations primarily handling employee requests unrelated to managed devices. Custom per-endpoint pricing; request a quote based on endpoint volume and selected modules. 7) Atera Atera combines RMM, PSA, and service desk capabilities with AI Copilot and IT Autopilot features for automated troubleshooting. Per-technician pricing varies by plan and billing term. G2 Rating: 4.6/5 Atera's Pricing Model Small IT teams (1-10 technicians) needing combined endpoint management and service desk without per-endpoint cost escalation evaluate Atera's per-technician pricing structure. Key Capabilities AI Copilot and IT Autopilot for automated troubleshooting and remediation Combined RMM, PSA, and service desk in a single platform Per-technician pricing eliminates cost escalation as managed endpoints grow Remote monitoring with automated alerting Consideration: Per-technician pricing can become more expensive as the technician team grows, so larger teams should compare total costs against per-endpoint alternatives. 8) SysAid SysAid positions itself as AI-first, embedding automation and AI assistance into existing workflows across chat, email, and self-service portals. The platform offers both cloud and on-premise deployment options. G2 Rating: 4.5/5 Gartner Peer Reviews Score: 4.6 SysAid's Deployment Flexibility Internal IT teams prioritizing high ticket deflection with flexible deployment requirements evaluate SysAid for its AI-first positioning and on-premise option that addresses compliance requirements preventing some organizations from using cloud-only solutions. Key Capabilities AI Copilot embedded across all service channels including chat, email, and self-service Cloud and on-premise deployment options Self-service deflection enabling end users to resolve issues without creating tickets Integration with Azure AD, Google, Okta, Slack, and Teams Consideration: Enterprise pricing without transparent published rates requires sales engagement to evaluate cost fit. 9) Zoho Desk Zoho Desk offers accessible entry pricing starting at $7/agent/month, with Zia AI providing sentiment analysis, auto-tagging, reply suggestions, and anomaly detection. A free tier supports up to 3 agents. G2 Rating: 4.4/5 Gartner Peer Reviews Score: 4.5 Zoho Desk's Value Positioning Small remote teams and startups needing AI-enabled ticketing evaluate Zoho Desk for its entry-level pricing with AI features available in middle tiers rather than locked behind enterprise pricing. Key Capabilities Zia AI for sentiment analysis, auto-tagging, and reply suggestions Free tier for up to 3 agents Integration with Zoho CRM, Books, and other Zoho products Multi-channel support across email, chat, and social Consideration: Strongest when used within the Zoho ecosystem; standalone deployment may lack integration depth with non-Zoho tools. 10) Pylon Pylon operates as a purpose-built B2B support platform for teams managing external customer support through Slack Connect and shared channels. The platform offers both autonomous AI Agents and AI Assistants (Copilots) for human agents, plus an Account Intelligence layer. Pylon's B2B Positioning B2B companies managing external customer support through Slack Connect and shared channels evaluate Pylon for its focus on multi-account scenarios and unified inbox capabilities. Key Capabilities AI Agents that resolve tickets autonomously end-to-end Unified inbox for Slack, Teams, email, and chat Account Intelligence layer with churn risk signals and health scores Designed for relatively fast initial deployment, with timing depending on integrations, data migration, and security requirements Consideration: B2B customer support focus rather than internal IT, HR, or employee support workflows. How AI Enhances Ticketing System Performance Purpose-built AI agents transform internal support operations by handling routine requests automatically while routing complex issues to the right specialists. This shift from manual triage to intelligent automation directly addresses the efficiency challenges remote teams face. The Role of Conversational AI in Modern Ticketing Conversational AI in ticketing systems understands request intent using large language models (LLMs) rather than relying on keyword matching or rigid decision trees. When an employee asks about updating their direct deposit information in Slack, the system recognizes this as an HR payroll request and can either resolve it automatically by referencing knowledge base articles or route it to the appropriate HR specialist. Platforms like Unthread's Agentic AI take this further by triggering workflows, escalating tickets, and updating external tools automatically based on natural language understanding. The AI can draft accurate responses before human handoff, reducing the time specialists spend on routine communications. Achieving High Deflection Rates with AI The most effective AI ticketing systems achieve meaningful deflection rates by addressing a broad range of internal support workflows, not just simple access requests. While some vendors emphasize high deflection by automating narrow use cases, platforms built for multi-department support handle requests across IT, HR, finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations. AI-assisted ticket workflows can reduce resolution time by accelerating classification, surfacing relevant context, and reducing manual triage. This improvement comes primarily through faster categorization and automated routing rather than simply deflecting easy tickets. Organizations evaluating AI ticketing platforms should examine which ticket types the AI handles, not just the overall deflection percentage. A deflection rate should be evaluated alongside the number of supported departments, ticket complexity, resolution quality, and the amount of specialist time saved. Seamless Communication: Ticketing Systems Built for Collaboration Remote teams waste significant time switching between communication platforms and ticketing systems. When employees must leave Slack to submit a ticket in a separate portal, then check that portal for updates, friction accumulates and response times suffer. Eliminating Context-Switching with Native Integrations Slack-native ticketing eliminates this friction by converting conversations into trackable tickets directly within the communication platform. Employees chat normally while the system tracks everything as tickets in the background, complete with SLA tracking, assignments, and escalations. This approach differs fundamentally from Slack integrations that simply notify users about tickets created elsewhere. With native Slack ticketing, the entire ticket lifecycle occurs within Slack: viewing the inbox, updating status, setting priority, closing tickets, and triggering automations all happen without opening external platforms. For remote teams, this matters because it preserves the conversational feel employees expect while providing the structured ticketing backend that internal support teams need. A channel like #it-help can function as a full internal help desk where some ticket types remain in-channel while others move to DMs or private flows for sensitive requests. Real-Time Collaboration for Distributed Teams AI ticketing platforms built for remote teams support asynchronous collaboration patterns. When a ticket requires input from multiple specialists across time zones, the system maintains context and surfaces relevant history automatically. Unthread's shared inbox accessible via Slack shows all open tickets with deep-linking to original threads, allowing team members to pick up conversations without searching through message history. This unified view ensures nothing falls through the cracks even when support staff work different hours. Open-Source vs. Proprietary: Choosing the Right Ticketing System The choice between open-source and proprietary ticketing systems involves tradeoffs in customization, cost, and AI capabilities that affect remote team operations. Evaluating Flexibility and Control Open-source ticketing systems can provide flexible ticketing and customization, but advanced AI automation may require additional integrations, development, and ongoing maintenance. Proprietary platforms with bring-your-own-LLM capabilities offer a middle path. Unthread's MCP integrations allow compatible AI assistants to securely access supported Unthread workspace data and actions, addressing vendor lock-in concerns while providing enterprise-grade AI features. Security and Compliance Considerations Remote teams handling internal support requests must consider where data resides and how AI models process sensitive information. Key security factors include: SOC2 Type II compliance for cloud-based platforms HIPAA compliance with BAAs for organizations handling protected health information On-premise deployment options for organizations with strict data residency requirements Privacy-first AI policies that do not train vendor models on customer data Commercial platforms often provide packaged compliance documentation and contractual security commitments, while self-hosted open-source deployments place more responsibility for configuration, auditing, and compliance on the organization. Streamlining IT Operations with Advanced Ticketing Software IT teams supporting remote workforces face unique challenges: distributed device fleets, varied network environments, and employees working across multiple time zones. AI ticketing systems address these challenges through intelligent automation and integrated endpoint management. Automating IT Workflows for Remote Support Effective IT ticketing for remote teams goes beyond basic ticket creation. Automation builders enable IT teams to create complex workflows triggered by Slack messages, emoji reactions, slash commands, or ticket events without requiring code. Common automated IT workflows include: Priority escalations that route urgent infrastructure issues to on-call specialists Employee account provisioning triggered by HR onboarding tickets Alert routing from monitoring tools into the ticketing system with automatic categorization Macro deployment for common troubleshooting steps These automations reduce manual intervention while ensuring consistent response times regardless of when requests arrive. Integrating with Existing IT Infrastructure AI ticketing platforms integrate with existing IT tools including Jira, GitHub, Asana, Linear, Okta, and Azure. This integration depth matters for remote IT teams who need ticketing workflows connected to change management, code deployment, and identity management systems. Bidirectional sync capabilities ensure that tickets created in Slack appear in systems of record for organizations maintaining those platforms alongside Slack-native tools. This hybrid approach allows teams to adopt conversational ticketing without abandoning existing investments. Beyond IT Support: Ticketing for HR and RevOps Teams Internal support extends far beyond IT help desks. HR teams manage employee queries about benefits, payroll, and policies. RevOps teams coordinate cross-functional operations. Finance teams handle expense questions and procurement requests. Each function benefits from structured ticketing with AI automation. Transforming HR Service Delivery with AI Ticketing HR teams handling remote employees face particular challenges around sensitive requests. Employees need to ask about parental leave policies, request pay stubs, or report workplace concerns without those conversations being visible to colleagues. Private ticketing capabilities enable HR teams to receive sensitive requests through Slack while maintaining confidentiality. When an employee DMs a question about their benefits or submits a request through a private channel, the system creates a ticket that only authorized HR staff can see. Common HR use cases for AI ticketing include: Payroll questions automatically routed to the appropriate payroll specialist Benefits enrollment requests linked to relevant documentation Employee document requests (W-2s, verification letters) fulfilled through automated workflows Policy questions resolved via knowledge base deflection Optimizing RevOps Workflows RevOps teams coordinate cross-functional operations spanning sales, marketing, and customer success. These teams often receive requests through multiple channels and struggle to track request status and ownership. AI ticketing provides structured intake and routing for RevOps requests while maintaining the conversational interface that cross-functional stakeholders expect. Automated workflows can trigger CRM updates, create tasks in project management tools, and escalate time-sensitive requests based on content analysis. Extending Internal Service Delivery Beyond Slack While this article focuses on internal support, some organizations need platforms that handle both internal employee requests and external customer inquiries. AI ticketing systems with omnichannel capabilities can serve both needs through unified platforms. Improving Employee Experience with Intelligent Responses AI-powered response generation draws from knowledge bases and previous ticket resolutions to draft accurate responses quickly. This capability reduces response time while maintaining quality, which can improve the employee service experience and reduce delays for internal teams. Customer portal and live chat capabilities extend AI ticketing beyond Slack to external-facing channels when needed. Embeddable widgets for websites provide branded chat interfaces that sync to Slack in real-time, allowing teams to manage interactions from a single platform. The Future of Self-Service in Internal Operations Employee self-service portals reduce internal ticket volume by helping staff find approved answers independently. AI enhances self-service by surfacing relevant articles based on query intent rather than keyword matching. The most effective self-service implementations combine: AI-powered search that understands natural language queries Contextual article suggestions based on user role and previous interactions Automatic escalation when self-service fails to resolve the issue Feedback loops that identify gaps in documentation Building a Smarter Knowledge Base with Self-Learning AI Traditional knowledge bases require manual content creation and maintenance, which internal support teams rarely have capacity to prioritize. Self-learning AI changes this equation by automatically generating and updating documentation based on ticket patterns. AI-Driven Content Creation Self-learning knowledge base systems detect repeat questions from ticket history and generate draft help articles for team review. Rather than starting from blank pages, support teams review AI-generated drafts and approve them with minor edits. This approach addresses a fundamental challenge: the people who know the answers (support specialists) rarely have time to write documentation, while the people asking questions generate clear signals about what documentation needs to exist. The AI Knowledge Manager Agent in platforms like Unthread automatically: Identifies frequently repeated questions from ticket data Drafts help articles based on successful resolution patterns Flags outdated documentation when ticket patterns indicate information gaps Shows clear before/after changes for one-click approval Ensuring Up-to-Date Information Knowledge bases become stale quickly, especially when processes change or tools are updated. AI gap analysis identifies issues where existing documentation no longer matches current procedures by analyzing ticket resolution patterns. When employees consistently ask questions that existing documentation should answer, the system flags those articles for review. This proactive approach keeps knowledge bases current without requiring manual audits. Implementing and Scaling AI Ticketing Solutions Enterprise deployment of AI ticketing requires careful attention to security, compliance, and integration with existing identity and HR systems. The implementation approach differs significantly from small team deployments. Key Considerations for Enterprise Deployment Organizations evaluating enterprise AI ticketing should assess: Slack Enterprise Grid support for large organizations with multiple workspaces SSO integration with existing identity providers SCIM sync for automated user provisioning and deprovisioning HRIS integration for employee directory synchronization Custom integrations via API for internal systems Dedicated hosting options for data residency requirements Unthread's Enterprise plan addresses these requirements with custom integrations and dedicated solutions teams for onboarding rather than self-service setup. Ensuring Security and Compliance Remote teams handling internal support must maintain security standards equivalent to on-premise operations. Key compliance requirements include: SOC2 Type II certification with regular independent security audits Penetration testing performed regularly HIPAA compliance with Business Associate Agreements for healthcare organizations Privacy-first AI that does not train vendor models on customer data Isolated hosted environments for organizations requiring dedicated infrastructure Unthread offers enterprise security options such as HIPAA support with BAAs and dedicated hosting through custom enterprise arrangements. Its MCP integrations also let compatible AI assistants interact with supported workspace data and actions. Free and Cost-Effective Ticketing Systems Small teams and startups need AI ticketing capabilities without enterprise budgets. Several platforms offer free tiers or accessible entry pricing that provides core functionality for growing organizations. Finding the Right Balance Budget-conscious organizations should evaluate which features they actually need versus which sound impressive but add unnecessary cost. Essential capabilities for small remote teams include: Slack or Teams integration for low-friction ticket creation Basic AI features like auto-categorization and suggested responses SLA tracking to ensure nothing falls through the cracks Simple reporting on ticket volume and response times Platforms offering free tiers for small teams include Jira Service Management (up to 3 agents) and Zoho Desk (up to 3 agents). These free tiers provide real functionality for testing AI ticketing before committing to paid plans. Growing Support with Scalable Options The ideal starting platform offers clear upgrade paths as teams grow. Organizations should consider: Per-agent pricing that scales predictably with team size Feature availability at each pricing tier Minimum seat requirements that may force over-purchasing Implementation support included or available as add-on Unthread's Basic plan starts at $50/agent/month with a minimum of 5 seats, providing conversation tracking, SLAs, assignments, and basic integrations. The Pro plan at $75/agent/month adds AI automation builder, self-learning documentation, and advanced analytics. Measuring Success: AI Analytics for Optimization AI ticketing platforms provide analytics capabilities that help remote teams identify bottlenecks, track performance trends, and demonstrate the value of support investments. Quantifying AI's Impact Key metrics for evaluating AI ticketing effectiveness include: AI deflection rate: Percentage of tickets resolved by AI or knowledge base without human intervention Mean time to first response: How quickly employees receive initial acknowledgment Mean time to resolution: Total time from ticket creation to closure SLA compliance: Percentage of tickets resolved within defined service levels Recurring issue patterns: Topics that generate repeated tickets indicating documentation gaps Unthread's AI Analytics provides real-time tracking of support volume, SLA breaches, and recurring issue patterns with automatic grouping and trend analysis. The platform shows AI deflection rates so teams can measure automation effectiveness. Data-Driven Decisions Analytics capabilities should support decision-making beyond simple reporting. Useful analytical features include: Custom dashboards showing metrics relevant to different stakeholders Export capabilities to BI tools like Looker, Tableau, or Hex via raw data API Slack-native summary sharing with SLA breach alerts delivered directly to channels Gap analysis identifying documentation needs based on ticket patterns Performance benchmarking across teams and time periods Remote support leaders use these analytics to justify headcount decisions, identify training needs, and demonstrate operational improvements to leadership. The ability to show documented ticket deflection or measurable reduction in resolution time provides concrete evidence of AI ticketing ROI. Why Unthread Leads the Internal Support Category Unthread earned the top ranking for its Slack-native internal support model, broad workflow automation, and documented Lemonade case study reporting about 40% automatic ticket resolution. The platform serves organizations from seed-stage startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, providing structured ticketing, AI automation, and knowledge management without requiring employees to leave Slack. The combination of conversational ticketing , self-learning knowledge bases , visual and code-based automation , and AI-powered deflection positions Unthread as a comprehensive internal support platform for remote-first organizations. Teams handling IT, HR, finance, legal, procurement, and workplace operations benefit from a unified system that eliminates tool-switching overhead while maintaining the conversational interface employees prefer. Organizations seeking to improve internal support delivery, reduce resolution times, and automate routine requests should evaluate Unthread's Basic, Pro, and Enterprise plans to determine which configuration best fits their remote team's needs. Frequently Asked Questions How does an AI ticketing system improve remote team collaboration? AI ticketing systems improve collaboration by keeping conversations and ticket management within the communication platforms remote teams already use. Rather than requiring employees to switch between Slack and a separate helpdesk portal, Slack-native platforms convert conversations into trackable tickets without disrupting workflow. AI handles routing, categorization, and initial responses automatically, ensuring requests reach the right specialists regardless of time zone differences. What are the key differences between a traditional help desk and an AI-powered ticketing system? Traditional help desks require manual ticket creation, categorization, and routing. Employees must learn a separate interface and check it for updates. AI-powered ticketing systems automate these tasks: tickets are created automatically from conversations, categorized based on content analysis, routed to appropriate specialists, and often resolved without human intervention. AI-assisted workflows can reduce resolution time by accelerating classification, surfacing relevant context, and reducing manual triage. Can AI ticketing systems integrate with existing communication platforms like Slack? Yes, though integration depth varies significantly. Some platforms offer Slack integrations that send notifications when tickets are created elsewhere. Slack-native platforms like Unthread operate entirely within Slack, converting threads into tickets and managing the full ticket lifecycle without requiring users to access external portals. This native approach eliminates context-switching and maintains the conversational interface employees prefer. What kind of ROI can organizations expect from implementing an AI ticketing system? ROI varies based on current support volume and processes. Organizations with documented case studies report significant automatic ticket resolution across multiple departments. Lemonade's documented case study shows Unthread resolves about 40% of tickets automatically. AI-assisted workflows can reduce resolution time by accelerating classification and surfacing relevant context. These improvements translate directly to support team capacity: handling more requests without adding headcount, or redirecting specialist time from routine tickets to complex issues requiring expertise. Are AI ticketing systems secure and compliant for sensitive data? Leading AI ticketing platforms maintain enterprise security standards including SOC2 Type II compliance, regular penetration testing, and HIPAA compliance with Business Associate Agreements for healthcare organizations. Key security considerations include where data resides, whether AI models are trained on customer data (privacy-first platforms do not), and whether organizations can use their own LLMs rather than sending sensitive information to third-party providers. Unthread's security approach includes SOC2 Type II compliance, penetration testing, and enterprise options such as HIPAA support with BAAs and dedicated hosting through custom arrangements. Unthread's MCP integrations also let compatible AI assistants interact with supported workspace data and actions.

title: Century Therapeutics Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Updates
summary: Completed pre-IND meeting with the FDA for CNTY-813, an iPSC-derived islet replacement therapy with functional cure potential in type 1 diabetes (T1D); IND submission on track for 4Q 2026 CNTY-813 preclinical data from oral presentation at ADA 2026 showed durable glucose control in vivo, immune
body_text: PDF Version Completed pre-IND meeting with the FDA for CNTY-813, an iPSC-derived islet replacement therapy with functional cure potential in type 1 diabetes (T1D); IND submission on track for 4Q 2026 CNTY-813 preclinical data from oral presentation at ADA 2026 showed durable glucose control in vivo, immune evasion, and manufacturing success at clinical scale, advancing its potential as a functional cure for T1D Upcoming oral presentations at European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD 2026) and Breakthrough T1D® Clinical & Research Congress 2026 highlighting CNTY-813 Company remains on track to advance CNTY-308, a CD19-targeted CAR-iT cell therapy with Allo-Evasion™ 5.0 into the clinic this year Cash runway into 1Q 2029 with cash, cash equivalents, and investments of $197.2 million as of June 30, 2026 PHILADELPHIA, Aug. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Century Therapeutics, Inc. (‘Century’, NASDAQ: IPSC), a biotechnology company developing induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cell therapies for autoimmune diseases, including T1D, and cancer, today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, and recent business highlights. "We are executing with speed against key development milestones, reinforcing our confidence in delivering on our ambition to transform diseases like T1D by creating functional cures at scale," said Brent Pfeiffenberger, Pharm.D., Chief Executive Officer of Century Therapeutics. "With CNTY-813, our preclinical data at ADA 2026 continue to support its potential as a functional T1D cure, and we have established our Phase 1 manufacturing process, demonstrating consistent product quality across independent batches. Our recent pre-IND meeting with the FDA builds on that progress yielding alignment with the FDA on our nonclinical data package, manufacturing strategy, and proposed Phase 1/2 trial design, keeping CNTY-813's IND submission on track for the fourth quarter of 2026. In addition, CNTY-308 remains on track to enter the clinic in 2026." Second Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights Pre-IND meeting with the FDA supports regulatory and initial clinical path for CNTY-813 Following a recent pre-IND meeting with the FDA, Century remains on track to submit an IND for CNTY-813 in the fourth quarter of 2026. Century and the FDA reached general alignment on the nonclinical data package, the proposed Phase 1 manufacturing process and the Phase 1/2 clinical trial design which includes alignment on: GLP toxicology study, which is ongoing and on track to support the planned submission. Phase 1 manufacturing process and testing plan that includes cell bank, intermediate, and final drug product release tests. Proposed Phase 1/2 clinical trial including dosing and patient eligibility criteria. New preclinical data further support CNTY-813 as a potential functional cure for T1D ; data were presented at the 2026 American Diabetes Association (ADA) Scientific Sessions in June (link to press release HERE ). Data demonstrated key advancements for CNTY-813 including: Durable in vivo glucose control maintained for more than eight months and immune evasion under allogeneic immune pressure without immunosuppression. Consistent and scalable product quality and performance at Phase 1 clinical trial scale. IND submission remains on track for 4Q 2026, with initial clinical data expected in 2H 2027. CNTY-813 Phase 1 manufacturing process established Century has established its Phase 1 clinical manufacturing bioreactor process for CNTY-813, demonstrating consistent process performance and product quality, endocrine purity, and optimal islet cell content across independent batches run at the same scale intended for the Phase 1 clinical trial. CNTY-813 preclinical data selected for oral presentations at congresses this fall 62nd Annual Meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD 2026; Milan, Italy; Presentation #225, Paris Hall, October 2nd, 2026, 10-11 AM CEST) Breakthrough T1D® Clinical & Research Congress 2026 (CRC 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; Presentation #341, Hall 1, October 9th, 2026, 3:50- 4:50 PM EST) Both presentations will highlight CNTY-813, Century's iPSC-derived islet replacement therapy program engineered with Allo-Evasion™ 5.0 for patients with T1D. CNTY - 308 clinical trial planned to initiate in 2026 Century remains on track, after aligning on nonclinical, manufacturing and Phase 1 clinical trial parameters with health authorities, to complete IND-enabling activities for CNTY-308, a CD19-targeted CD4⁺/CD8⁺ αβ CAR-iT cell therapy engineered with Allo-Evasion™ 5.0 for B-cell-mediated diseases. CNTY-308 is anticipated to enter the clinic in 2026. Preclinical data showed functional comparability to primary CAR-T cells, including target-driven proliferation, cytokine secretion, and durable persistence. Collectively, these results and the expanding clinical validation of CAR-T therapy support Century’s confidence that CNTY-308 could deliver autologous-like benefits in an allogeneic, patient-centric format designed to broaden access. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Cash Position: Cash, cash equivalents, and investments were $197.2 million as of June 30, 2026, as compared to $117.1 million as of December 31, 2025. The company estimates its cash, cash equivalents, and investments as of June 30, 2026 will support operations into 1Q 2029. Research and Development (R&D) Expenses: R&D expenses were $19.6 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $26.9 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily the result of a reduction in personnel and a reduction in facility costs as a result of our previously announced portfolio prioritization. General and Administrative (G&A) Expenses: G&A expenses were $5.8 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $7.8 million for the same period in 2025. Net Income (Loss): Net (loss) was $34.6 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to net (loss) of $32.5 million for the same period in 2025. About Century Therapeutics Century Therapeutics (NASDAQ: IPSC) is a biotechnology company advancing a pipeline of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cell therapies with the potential to meaningfully address autoimmune diseases, including type 1 diabetes, and cancer. Century’s therapies are derived from its iPSC cell foundry and leverage its novel immune evasion engineering technology, Allo-Evasion™. Century believes its approach to developing off-the-shelf cell therapies will expand patient access and provide advantages over existing cell therapies which will ultimately advance the course of care. For more information on Century Therapeutics, please visit www.centurytx.com and connect with us on LinkedIn.
